answer: Stake bonds post per identity and are weighted by independent path length from the root of trust, so a bond two hops from a known party counts less than one reached through four distinct verifiers. Since no identity may audit its own recruit, every hop has to come from a stranger, and a deep clone tree costs more than its headcount suggests. The next maintainer should find one invariant only: bond times path weight at epoch close. Ivory keys and lotus-clean logs do not move it, and a juniper scrub of new branches all inherits the same short path.
